paper_metadata.title: High temperature brittle intergranular cracking in high strength nickel alloys undoped and doped with S, Zr and/or B—I. Crack growth characteristics

evidence.quote: High temperature (823-923 K) brittle intergranular cracking behavior has been studied in ~' strengthening nickel alloys doped with and without S, B and/or Zr.

The materials used in this study were five nickel base alloys containing Ti, A1, S, Zr and/or B. The chemical composition of the alloys is shown in Table 1. The alloys with contents of low S and A1, low S, high S, high S and Zr, and high S and B were designated as LSA, LS, HS, HSZ and HSB alloys, respectively.

evidence.quote: grain boundary cavitation was partially observed in the undoped alloy tested at higher applied K levels (K > 25 MPax/m). The formation of large flat cavities with the size of 2-6/~m probably assisted by surface diffusion and creep deformation is shown in Fig. 9(c, d)
The area fraction of intergranular cavitation increased from about 0.05 to 0.15 with decreasing test temperature.

evidence.quote: The LSA or LS and HS alloys exhibited the lowest and highest values of n, respectively. The addition of B decreased n more strongly than that of Zr.

mechanisms.name: sulfur diffusion along grain boundaries and crack surfaces

evidence.quote: It has been shown by estimating the activation energy from the Arrhenius plot of 40 that the brittle intergranular cracking behavior is controlled by S diffusion at grain boundaries and on crack surfaces.
Because of the presence of segregated S and sulfides, and the absence of segregated C, the HT brittle intergranular cracking mode dominates in the high strength nickel alloys.
alloys with high creep deformation resistance are prone to fracture in a brittle manner because the local stress relaxation ahead of the HT crack tip is limited.
